title: Code Factory: Polyglot Evidence for AI-Built Code
description:
Your AI writes the change. Code Factory shows what was actually checked. Core 0.50.0 expands the configured native security worker to 30 rules across 12 declared languages, adds frozen JSON/SARIF 2.1.0 and opt-in pre-commit, and connects signed-observation verify_claim, a bounded Proof Agent and the Devin evidence plugin. Review exact mutation diffs, source-bound receipts and actionable gaps without handing release authority to an agent. Editor and Devin plugins target 1.3.6.

Current coverage adds Go/Java/C#/Ruby framework sources and sinks plus wider Ruby/Swift trust checks. New request rules are review-tier; the shipped variant has no fresh precision score. Round 7 below is the earlier ruleset. See docs/evidence/polyglot-coverage-round8.json.

Historical Round 7 supported 38/40 decided default-tier alerts (95.0%; Wilson 95% 83.5–98.6%), with 12 additional unclear; review tier supported 23/40 (57.5%), with 3 unclear. Advisory recall was 0/161. Six languages had insufficient precision samples. AI labels do not establish twelve-language accuracy or independent human validation. Per-language evidence is in docs/evidence/polyglot-readiness-round7.json. The earlier Round 6 90% panel is a separate sampling design, not a comparable improvement. The Python-only local quick scan and configured native worker have distinct coverage. No overall scan-speed gain is claimed.

The read-only Agent Proof Bridge and review-required Proof Worklog preserve scope and evidence boundaries. The deterministic AppForge App Review evidence gate retains 30 policy and release-risk checks and named human control; it does not guarantee approval or claim a measured rejection-rate reduction. Supplied observations are not provider certification, production proof, security certification or release authority.
